On-Chain Operator. Lesson 10.2, Cash-and-carry basis trades. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You already split base yield from emissions. Advanced yield still starts with that split, then names a more particular engine.
In rising markets, dated futures usually trade above spot.
The gap (basis) shrinks to zero at expiry because the future settles at spot.
Buy spot + short the future at the same size and you lock that gap, whatever the price does, as long as both legs survive to expiry.
Work the example on paper. ETH spot 3,000, 90-day future 3,060. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.

Work the example on paper. At expiry, if ETH is 2,000: spot leg −1,000, short future +1,060 → +60 per ETH. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
Work the example on paper. At expiry, if ETH is 4,500: spot leg +1,500, short future −1,440 → +60 per ETH. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.

On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Both legs opened together, same size. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Futures margin survives at least a +100% move, or a rule to top up. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Venue risk sized (cap per venue). If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Plan to hold to expiry; early exit may be at a worse basis. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
Check yourself. 1. Spot 2,000, 180-day future 2,080. Annualised basis? The answer: 4% × 365/180 ≈ 8.1%.
Check yourself. 2. Why is the return "locked" at expiry? The answer: The future settles at spot, so the gain on one leg offsets the loss on the other, leaving the entry basis.
Check yourself. 3. What breaks the trade before expiry? The answer: A margin call or liquidation on the short future during a rally, or venue failure.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to capture the premium of a dated future over spot without taking a view on price.
annualised basis = (future divided by spot minus 1) times 365 divided by days.
